clue.text: Distraught chap finds his newspaper no longer covers this

indicators.note: someone distraught is all over the place, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A man is upset to find his paper has stopped carrying some topic he cared about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distraught' scrambles CHAP FINDS HIS. The definition recalls the old British habit of wrapping takeaway fish and chips in yesterday's newspaper, which hygiene rules ended.
explanation.definitionFit: The British chip-shop meal was traditionally wrapped in old newsprint, a practice since abandoned.

clue.text: Performer who should certainly take a bow?

definitions.text: Performer who should certainly take a bow?

parts.words: Performer who should certainly take a bow?
parts.note: a performer earning applause takes a bow, but this musician literally picks up a bow to play the violin

explanation.surface: A performer who has done so well they surely deserve applause.
explanation.walkthrough: The bow seems to be the end-of-show curtsey; it is the stick drawn across violin strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A violinist, colloquially a fiddle player, must take up a bow to perform at all.

clue.text: Airs and graces initially adopted by children

indicators.note: something adopted is taken into a family, so one letter is taken into the children's word

parts.note: sons are male children

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word graces

explanation.surface: Children pick up affected manners and pretensions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Airs and graces' reads as one phrase about snobbery, but 'Airs' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune or melody, so airs are pieces sung.

clue.text: Tragic figure from Greece eating no bananas

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so these letters go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Greek tragic heroine who refuses to eat bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' seems to be food; it is the slang word for mad, signalling an anagram of EATING NO.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the heroine of Sophocles' Greek tragedy who buries her brother and is condemned to death.

clue.text: 500 helpers for Santa mostly in burrow

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: Santa's helpers are traditionally elves

explanation.surface: Hundreds of Santa's elves tunnelling underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of ELVES to leave ELVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To delve is to dig or search deeply, much as one burrows into something.

clue.text: Do housework, annoyed about current obstruction

parts.note: to hoover is British usage for vacuum-cleaning, a household chore

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for annoyed is read backwards

parts.note: mad can mean angry or annoyed

explanation.surface: Someone cross about having to do the cleaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns MAD into DAM. The current is a river's flow, not electricity or the present.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hoover Dam blocks the Colorado River, so it obstructs a water current.

clue.text: Friend on TV has hope dashed live

indicators.note: something dashed is smashed to pieces, so the letters of hope are rearranged

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: A character on a TV show sees their hopes shattered during a live broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dashed' rearranges HOPE into PHOE.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoebe Buffay is one of the six title characters of the sitcom Friends.

clue.text: After unfinished dessert, also called for Greek casserole

indicators.note: after places the alias abbreviation behind the shortened dessert
unfinished means its last letter is cut off

parts.note: mousse is a light whipped dessert
aka is the standard abbreviation for also known as

explanation.surface: A menu note: after the dessert left half-eaten, a Greek dish also known by another name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the final E of the dessert; 'After' places the alias abbreviation behind it, not in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Moussaka is a baked Greek dish of layered aubergine, minced meat and sauce.

clue.text: Charlie has synthetic material in drawer?

definitions.note: a noun read as one who draws: a tool for drawing

parts.note: Charlie is the radio code word for C
rayon is a man-made fibre

explanation.surface: Charlie has some artificial fabric tucked in a chest of drawers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' suggests furniture; read it as something that draws, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A crayon is a stick of coloured wax used for drawing pictures.

clue.text: Freely give two pounds over for a Renaissance man

parts.note: to donate is to give freely
L is the abbreviation for pound (libra), so two of them make LL
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Handing over a couple of pounds to a well-rounded Renaissance type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Renaissance man' usually means a polymath; here it is a literal artist of the period.
explanation.definitionFit: Donatello was a Florentine sculptor of the early Italian Renaissance.

clue.text: The Telegraph's hosting party, getting bouquet

indicators.note: a host takes guests in, so the paper's word contains the party word

parts.note: the clue is in the Telegraph, so the paper speaks of itself as ours
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: The newspaper throws a party and receives a bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouquet' looks floral; it is the wine-taster's word for smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's bouquet is its characteristic smell, an odour.

clue.text: Way to eat dip or a pasta dish

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road or way
a sag is a dip or droop

explanation.surface: A choice between how to eat a dip or a pasta dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dip' looks like a party snack; it is a sag in a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is an Italian baked dish of layered flat pasta sheets with meat and sauce.

clue.text: English setter's catching fish for diplomatic group

indicators.note: catching means holding, so the setter's word wraps round the fish

parts.note: the setter refers to themself, so 'setter's' gives my
bass is a kind of fish

explanation.surface: An English dog of the setter breed catching a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the dog; it is the crossword compiler, whose possessive is MY.
explanation.definitionFit: An embassy is the body of diplomats representing one state in another country.

clue.text: Foolish nerd liked getting excited again

indicators.note: foolish suggests silly disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A silly geek liked becoming worked up once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foolish' scrambles NERD LIKED.
explanation.definitionFit: To rekindle a feeling is to arouse or stir it again after it died down.

clue.text: A thousand quid going on small undergarments

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, as in kilo
nicker is British slang for a pound sterling, as is quid
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Spending a thousand pounds on tiny underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quid' and 'nicker' are both British slang for a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Knickers are women's underpants, a kind of undergarment.

clue.text: Barnet Hospital welcoming US university's key specialist

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the hair-and-hospital letters enclose the university

parts.note: Barnet, from rhyming slang Barnet Fair, is London slang for hair, i.e. locks
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: A hospital in Barnet, north London, receives a leading American university's expert.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is a London borough, but Cockney rhyming slang 'Barnet Fair' means hair, giving LOCKS.
explanation.definitionFit: A locksmith makes and repairs locks and cuts keys, a specialist in keys.

clue.text: Tedious person's baguette?

definitions.meaning: the French word for bread, and a baguette is French bread

explanation.surface: A bore described as a loaf of French bread.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second sense is French, not English.
explanation.definitionFit: A pain in the neck is a bore, and French bakers call their bread pain.

clue.text: Good Scottish fabric dressing old, repulsive figure

indicators.note: dressing means clothing something, so the fabric wraps round the letter for old

parts.note: Argyle is a diamond-patterned knit named after a Scottish clan

explanation.surface: Fine Scottish cloth used to clothe an ugly old person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' puts ARGYLE around O to make ARGOYLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gargoyle is a grotesque carved creature, so the word also describes an ugly person.

clue.text: Losing grand, regretting impoverishment

indicators.note: losing means doing without, so one letter is taken away

parts.note: ruing means regretting
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A gambler who loses a thousand and regrets the poverty that follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing' drops G from RUING.
explanation.definitionFit: Financial ruin is the state of having lost all one's money.

clue.text: What Turner does, if not around gallery

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the word for 'if not' is read backwards

parts.note: or means 'if not', as in do it or else
Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: A question about the painter J.M.W. Turner and whether he would be absent from the Tate.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner seems to be the painter, whose works hang in the Tate gallery; read it as anything that turns. 'around' reads the 'if not' word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to turn, which is what any turner does.

clue.text: I didn't hear that business heartlessly made a profit

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: heartlessly means without the middle letters, keeping the ends of the word made

parts.note: gain means profit

explanation.surface: Someone didn't catch a remark about a company ruthlessly turning a profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' takes the middle out of MADE to leave ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Come again? is a colloquial request to repeat something you missed.

clue.text: Close match? It goes on at the end of the day

definitions.text: It goes on at the end of the day

parts.note: nigh means near or close
a tie is a sports fixture or match

explanation.surface: A tight sporting contest that runs on until nightfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes on' looks like a match continuing; it means put on, as clothing at bedtime.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is a nightdress, worn to bed in the evening.

clue.text: Grass where schoolchildren might be found

definitions.meaning: to grass is British slang for ... on someone to the police
pupils sit in a form, a British school class

explanation.surface: Children playing on a school lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is not a lawn but slang for snitching; a form is a British school year group.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform on someone is to tell the authorities about them.

clue.text: Cheers rulers providing income

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks, like cheers
kings are rulers

explanation.surface: A toast to monarchs who bring in the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' is thanks, not a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Takings are the money a business receives, its revenue.

clue.text: Enjoying a bit of archaeology

definitions.meaning: archaeologists excavate, so a dig is part of the work

explanation.surface: Someone having fun on an archaeological dig.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig something is slang for liking it, and excavation is the core activity of archaeologists.

clue.text: Money gleaned from education

indicators.note: gleaned means gathered out of, so the letters are picked from inside the word

explanation.surface: Wealth acquired through schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gleaned from' takes the letters inside eDUCATion.
explanation.definitionFit: A ducat was a gold coin used across Europe, so it is a form of money.

clue.text: Date in Rome — time that is for the locals

parts.note: the ides was a date in the ancient Roman calendar, mid-month

explanation.surface: A date in the Roman calendar, with time for the local people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the locals' refers back to Rome: the answer is Latin, what Romans would say.
explanation.definitionFit: Id est is the Latin phrase, abbreviated i.e., meaning that is, used by Romans.

clue.text: Elephant's tail close to trunk

indicators.note: a tail is the hind end, so the last letter of the word is taken

parts.note: or so means approximately, close to a figure

explanation.surface: An elephant's tail lies near its trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The trunk looks like the elephant's nose; it is the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the human body's trunk, without head or limbs.

clue.text: Long bits of verse about Yankee's restless feeling

indicators.note: about means around, so the long-and-verse words surround the letter

parts.note: to itch for something is to long for it
feet are the metrical units of a line of verse
Yankee is the radio code word for Y

explanation.surface: Lengthy lines of poetry about an American and his wanderlust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes the long-plus-verse pair wrap round the Yankee letter; 'Long' is a verb meaning yearn, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Itchy feet is an idiom for an urge to travel or move on.

clue.text: Dramas here are besetting politician struck by passion

indicators.note: besetting means surrounding on all sides, so the word are wraps round the rest

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
hit means struck
heat means passion or intensity

explanation.surface: Plays are full of politicians beset by passion and lashing out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'besetting' splits the word 'are' into A and RE round the politician, struck and passion pieces; 'Dramas here' is the definition, the place plays are staged.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphitheatre is an open-air venue where plays and spectacles are staged.
